title: Fly to Khunjerab, the roof of the Karakoram Highway
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: At the far northern tip of Pakistan, on the border with China, lies the Khunjerab Pass.
Let's fly up the valley from the Pakistani side, along the Karakoram Highway.
The road climbs through the Khunjerab National Park, set up in nineteen seventy-nine.
The park was created to protect rare animals like the Marco Polo sheep, the snow leopard and the blue sheep.
And there it is: the Khunjerab Pass, at nearly four thousand seven hundred metres.
It is often described as the highest paved international border crossing in the world.
The road over the pass was fully paved in nineteen eighty-two, as part of the Karakoram Highway.
Across the border is China's Xinjiang region. Kashgar is about four hundred and eighteen kilometres away.
At the border, traffic switches sides: Pakistanis drive on the left, Chinese drivers on the right.
Heavy snow closes the road to most traffic for several months each winter.
The pass is a symbol of Pakistan-China friendship, and a vital trade link between the two countries.
